reason: E2 directly supports that ultrafine-grain microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi enhances oxidation resistance via chromia/alumina formation and internal oxidation, but E1 shows that in CrMnFeCoNi, Mn-oxides dominate and no Cr2O3 forms, contradicting the premise that refinement universally favors protective over non-protective oxidation. The hypothesis overgeneralizes from E2 and ignores the conflicting behavior in E1, leaving key premises about Mn-oxide suppression and universal protective scale formation unsupported.
premises: Ultrafine-grained microstructure enhances grain boundary diffusion and elemental homogenization in HEAs.
Enhanced diffusion of Cr and Al to the surface promotes continuous protective chromia/alumina scales.
Continuous protective oxide scales improve structural and chemical stability at high temperatures.
Coarse-grained HEAs form non-protective oxides (e.g., Mn-oxides) leading to instability.
Microstructural refinement suppresses non-protective oxidation in favor of protective scale formation.
